hubDemo.name: MapMaker Lessons (demo)
hubDemo.lessonsIntro: Ten lessons that teach Grade 8 US History with National Geographic MapMaker maps, arranged by topic in the order most courses teach them. Each one pairs a map with an inquiry, a Word student sheet in English and Spanish, and a separate teacher page with the answers.

theme.about: Site colours the publishing notebook sets on the Hub site (Esri Calcite blue). Only these keys are changed.

vera.name: Vera
vera.note: Vera's chat page. The Lessons page has an Ask Vera button; lesson pages link to it with the lesson pre-filled. No embeds.

classroom.about: Share to Google Classroom button on each lesson page. It shares the lesson's MapMaker map, never the lesson page, which holds the answer notes. Follows Google's Classroom branding guidelines: approved wording, the official icon on the left (32 to 96 px, unaltered), Roboto Bold, a 20% black shade on the icon on hover, and the trademark notice in the page footer. The button is left out if icon is empty.

aiPrompt.about: Prompt teachers can paste into the AI tool their school allows. The lesson's map, layers, bookmarks and questions are added after these rules, from the lesson file, so the prompt never names a layer the map doesn't have.
aiPrompt.label: Prompt for your own AI
rules: You are helping a teacher make classroom questions for a National Geographic MapMaker lesson. The map, its layers, what each pop-up shows, its bookmarks and the questions already written are listed below.

Use only the layers, pop-up contents and bookmarks listed. Do not invent layers, tools, data or map features. If a question would need information this map does not show, say so instead of inventing it.

Every question must be answerable by a student who opens the map in MapMaker and uses it: clicking pop-ups, reading the legend, using bookmarks, measuring or turning layers on and off. Name the exact layer or bookmark a student should use.
Write for grade 8 (age 13 to 14), in short sentences. Do not include answers unless the teacher asks for them, and never write material for students that contains the answers.

MapMaker has these tools: Basemaps, Open map, Map layers (turn layers on and off), Add layer, Legend, Measure (miles and feet), Sketch, 2D/3D, Bookmarks and pop-ups. It has no time slider or filter unless listed below. A pop-up that says 1 of 2 means more than one feature is at that spot; use the arrows to see each one.
